title: Read key=value pairs from a file, print them, look values up and free them
notes:
observed: re/original-grade-txt/32_kvs.grade.txt starts with `Attempting to compile:` and an EMPTY command, then three testcase blocks, each `Your output is correct` / `  - Valgrind was clean (no errors, no memory leaks)` / `valgrind was clean`, then `Overall Grade: A`. observed: the README fixes the four functions (readKVs/freeKVs/printKVs/lookupValue), the `key = '%s' value = '%s'
` print format, and says 'test them using the main in kv_test.c'; the Makefile's CFLAGS are `-Wall -Werror -std=gnu99 -pedantic -ggdb3` and its PROGRAM is `kv_test`; 32_kvs/test.txt is the fixture the driver reads. recovered: drivers/32_kvs/kv_test.c is the teacher driver - its content is the in-directory kv_test.c, and the object corroborates it (one function `main`, 238 bytes, at DWARF line 7; imports only readKVs/printKVs/lookupValue/freeKVs/printf/puts; .rodata "test.txt", "Printing all keys
", the five lookup keys and "lookupValue('%s')=%s
"). One divergence is recorded in the driver's header comment: the object imports `puts` and stores "Printing all keys
" with a single newline, so the teacher's original wrote the blank line with a separate puts("") call while the committed source writes printf("Printing all keys

"); the bytes printed are identical. inferred: the driver takes no arguments and reads a fixed file name, so the original's three testcases can only have been three identical runs of ./kv_test, which is what is configured; configs/expected/32_kvs/test.txt is the reference run's stdout (including `lookupValue('cantaloupe')=(null)` for the missing key, which is what both glibc and this libc print for a NULL %s). platform substitution: the 2024 grader used valgrind, which does not exist on macOS/arm64 and cannot be installed. `memory_check` now builds twice - AddressSanitizer for out-of-bounds/use-after-free/double-free, and a plain build under Apple's `leaks --atExit --` for leaked allocations - and the original valgrind wording is kept so the reports stay comparable. Neither engine reports uninitialised reads, which valgrind did. The reference implementation is clean under both passes. Template exclusions: the committed Linux `kv_test` binary, kv.o/kv_test.o and the stray test1.c/test1.txt are not part of the starting template; kv.c is reduced to the four signatures and kv.h keeps only the teacher's //DEFINE ME! comments.
